_about: Each cloud, layer by layer: the cloud's own service, the open option beside it, where the fact comes from and the day it was last checked. `qz cloud show <cloud>` prints a cloud; `qz cloud check` lists every fact older than max_age_days, so nobody builds on a stale one. Re-check a fact at its source, then change its text and its date together.

layers.gateway: The AI gateway: one way in for model calls
layers.identity: Who is asking, and how the app reaches the cloud's services

gateway_pattern: One way in: every model call goes through the gateway, which the agent reaches on localhost. The agent holds only the gateway's key.
It holds the keys: provider keys (where a cloud needs one) sit in the cloud's secret store and reach the gateway's container only.
It routes between models: the agent asks for agent-model; the gateway maps the name to the cloud's Claude and falls back to the cloud's open-weight model.
It caps spend: a budget on each paid model; once spent, calls go to the fallback.
It logs each call: model, tokens, cost and time, inside the run's trace, with no prompt or answer text.

azure.name: Microsoft Azure
azure.template: Azure Container Apps (the agent and the gateway in one app), Microsoft Foundry for the models, Key Vault for the keys

models.service: Microsoft Foundry: Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Claude Haiku 5.5, deployed as Global Standard and billed through the Azure Marketplace; version 2 of each is hosted on Azure. gpt-oss-120b is sold by Azure and needs a Foundry project.
models.open: gpt-oss-120b (Apache 2.0) in Foundry, or the open models on SIE in AKS (the Kubernetes template)

gateway.service: Azure API Management AI gateway: a token limit per minute or a quota per key (OpenAI, Anthropic Messages on the v2 tiers, Vertex AI), token metrics to Application Insights, semantic caching, content safety checks, backend load balancing with a circuit breaker
gateway.open: LiteLLM proxy (MIT) as a second container in the app: what the template runs

search.service: Foundry IQ (Azure AI Search): hybrid search (full text and vectors merged by Reciprocal Rank Fusion) with semantic ranking, and agentic retrieval, whose planning and answer synthesis are generally available in REST API 2026-10-01
search.open: The Studio's hybrid RAG kit in a container, or pgvector in a PostgreSQL the client runs

parsing.service: Azure Document Intelligence in Foundry Tools: the layout model returns Markdown (outputContentFormat=markdown) from PDFs, scans, images and Office files; Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools extracts fields
parsing.open: Docling, MinerU2.5-Pro or LightOnOCR-3 served by SIE on AKS

identity.service: Microsoft Entra ID: Foundry's Claude endpoint accepts Entra ID tokens or a deployment key; the container app reads Key Vault with its managed identity (Key Vault Secrets User), no key
identity.open: Keycloak (OIDC); the agent checks any OIDC provider's tokens (AGENT_IDENTITY=oidc)

secrets.service: Azure Key Vault: the container app names a secret by its versionless URL and reads it through its managed identity; a changed value reaches the app on a new revision or a restart
secrets.open: OpenBao (MPL-2.0, a Linux Foundation OpenSSF project), with External Secrets Operator on AKS

tracing.service: Azure Monitor: OTLP ingestion into Application Insights (through an OpenTelemetry Collector), or the Microsoft OpenTelemetry Distro; an Agents view built on the OpenTelemetry generative AI conventions
tracing.open: Langfuse, self-hosted, taking OTLP at /api/public/otel: where the starters send their traces

containers.service: Azure Container Apps: a sidecar is one more container in the app's template, sharing its network and disk; container app jobs run to completion

aws.name: Amazon Web Services
aws.template: Amazon ECS on Fargate (the agent and the gateway in one task), Amazon Bedrock for the models through the task's role, Secrets Manager for the keys

models.service: Amazon Bedrock: Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Claude Haiku 5.5 through inference profiles only (us., eu. and global.; Haiku also au. and jp.), called with the task's IAM role; gpt-oss-120b in-region as openai.gpt-oss-120b-1:0
models.open: gpt-oss-120b on Bedrock, or the open models on SIE in EKS

gateway.service: AWS publishes Guidance for a Multi-Provider Generative AI Gateway on AWS, built on LiteLLM, on ECS or EKS
gateway.open: LiteLLM proxy (MIT) as a second container in the task: what the template runs

search.service: Amazon OpenSearch Service and OpenSearch Serverless (hybrid search); Amazon S3 Vectors for low-cost vector storage, exportable to OpenSearch Serverless; both serve as Bedrock Knowledge Bases stores
search.open: OpenSearch (Apache 2.0) or pgvector, or the Studio's hybrid RAG kit

parsing.service: Amazon Bedrock Data Automation: document text with Markdown (the default), HTML or CSV tables; Amazon Textract with Layout
parsing.open: Docling, MinerU2.5-Pro or LightOnOCR-3 served by SIE on EKS

identity.service: Amazon Cognito user pools: an OIDC provider issuing JWTs, which also federates the client's SAML or OIDC workforce provider; the task role gives the gateway Bedrock with no key
identity.open: Keycloak (OIDC); the agent checks any OIDC provider's tokens (AGENT_IDENTITY=oidc)

secrets.service: AWS Secrets Manager: the task definition names each secret's ARN and the task execution role reads it when the task starts (secretsmanager:GetSecretValue, and kms:Decrypt for a customer key)
secrets.open: OpenBao (MPL-2.0, a Linux Foundation OpenSSF project), with External Secrets Operator on EKS

tracing.service: Amazon CloudWatch: an OTLP endpoint for traces (HTTP only, signed with SigV4, so a collector such as the AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry signs the calls) feeding Application Signals
tracing.open: Langfuse, self-hosted, taking OTLP at /api/public/otel: where the starters send their traces

containers.service: Amazon ECS on Fargate: in awsvpc mode the containers of one task talk over localhost; Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime is the managed host built for agents (runs up to 8 hours)

gcp.name: Google Cloud
gcp.template: Cloud Run (the agent and the gateway in one service), Claude on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform through the service account, Secret Manager for the keys

models.service: Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform (formerly Vertex AI) Model Garden: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (from 28 September 2026) and Claude Haiku 5.5 (from 7 October 2026) as managed APIs, called with the service account; gpt-oss-120b as gpt-oss-120b-maas on the global endpoint and us-central1
models.open: gpt-oss-120b on Agent Platform, or the open models on SIE in GKE

gateway.service: Apigee as an AI gateway: LLM token policies (token quotas and limits per app), semantic caching, and circuit breaking between model endpoints
gateway.open: LiteLLM proxy (MIT) as a sidecar in the Cloud Run service: what the template runs

search.service: Agent Retrieval (formerly Vector Search 2.0): managed collections with semantic, text and hybrid search, the embeddings made in the same call; Agent Search (formerly Vertex AI Search) for enterprise search
search.open: pgvector in a PostgreSQL the client runs, or the Studio's hybrid RAG kit

parsing.service: Document AI layout parser (processor type LAYOUT_PARSER_PROCESSOR): layout-aware chunks; through RAG Engine, at most 20 MB per file and 500 pages per PDF
parsing.open: Docling, MinerU2.5-Pro or LightOnOCR-3 served by SIE on GKE

identity.service: Identity-Aware Proxy signs each request it lets through with an ES256 JWT in x-goog-iap-jwt-assertion; the service account reaches Agent Platform with IAM, no key. The agent's OIDC check reads RS256 bearer tokens, so it sits behind the client's OIDC provider, not IAP's header
identity.open: Keycloak (OIDC); the agent checks any OIDC provider's RS256 tokens (AGENT_IDENTITY=oidc)

secrets.service: Secret Manager: Cloud Run sets a secret as an environment variable or mounts it as a file; the service's identity needs Secret Manager Secret Accessor
secrets.open: OpenBao (MPL-2.0, a Linux Foundation OpenSSF project), with External Secrets Operator on GKE

tracing.service: Cloud Trace through the Telemetry (OTLP) API at telemetry.googleapis.com, Google's recommended path; the Google-Built OpenTelemetry Collector runs as a Cloud Run sidecar and adds the credentials
tracing.open: Langfuse, self-hosted, taking OTLP at /api/public/otel: where the starters send their traces

containers.service: Cloud Run: one ingress container and sidecars in one instance, talking over localhost; Cloud Run jobs run to completion

kubernetes.name: Your own Kubernetes
kubernetes.template: A Deployment with the agent and the gateway in one pod, SIE from its Helm chart for the open models, External Secrets Operator bringing the keys from the cloud's secret store

models.service: SIE (Superlinked Inference Engine, Apache 2.0) serves the open models an agent calls through one OpenAI-compatible API, loading each on demand; the agent loop runs on qwen3.8-27b. Claude comes from the Claude API through the gateway
models.open: SIE is the open option itself

gateway.service: LiteLLM proxy (MIT) as a second container in the agent's pod; SIE has its own load-balancing gateway in front of its workers, which this one calls with SIE's token
gateway.open: LiteLLM is the open option itself

search.service: SIE serves the retrieval models (bge-m3, splade-v3, colbertv2, qwen3-reranker); the vectors live in the client's store or the Studio's hybrid RAG kit

parsing.service: SIE serves document-to-Markdown models: lightonocr-3, mineru (MinerU2.5-Pro), glm-ocr, paddleocr-vl and docling
parsing.open: The same models, all open weights

identity.service: The client's OIDC provider; the agent checks its RS256 tokens (AGENT_IDENTITY=oidc)
identity.open: Keycloak 26.6 (April 2026), which supports federated client authentication with Kubernetes service account tokens

secrets.service: External Secrets Operator copies each key from the cloud's secret store (AWS Secrets Manager, Azure Key Vault, Google Secret Manager) or OpenBao into a Kubernetes Secret, through a ClusterSecretStore and ExternalSecret resources (external-secrets.io/v1)
secrets.open: OpenBao (MPL-2.0, a Linux Foundation OpenSSF project)

tracing.service: Langfuse takes OTLP over HTTP at /api/public/otel (traces only, no gRPC); SIE ships Grafana dashboards for its own metrics
tracing.open: Langfuse self-hosted is the open option itself

containers.service: A Deployment with the agent and the gateway in one pod; SIE from its Helm chart (oci://ghcr.io/superlinked/charts/sie-cluster 0.11.1) with KEDA scale-to-zero; SIE's Terraform modules create GPU clusters on EKS, AKS, GKE and ACK
containers.open: Kubernetes and SIE are the open option themselves

sie._about: What the Kubernetes template sets on SIE's chart, and why: each of these is unsafe at the chart's default before 0.13.0. `qz cloud lint` fails when the template leaves any of them at its default.
